blocks.text: Most people search this phrase for one of two reasons. A designer sent you a brand font, or a font you bought won't show up in Canva. Either way, the upload happens inside Canva, not in macOS. You don't need a special Mac menu to add the font. The Mac part is mostly about the file. You need to find it, check it, and make sure it opens cleanly before you send it to Canva.
Requirements to upload a font to Canva

Canva limits font uploads by plan and by role. The core rules match across the guides I could check. Two details differ, so confirm them on your own account before you spend time on a failed upload. The list below covers every rule the sources agree on.

items: Plan: Canva Pro, Teams, Education or Nonprofits. One guide also lists Business.
Role: owner, admin or brand designer. One guide lists only owner and admin.
Format: static OTF, TTF or WOFF files.
Size: under 15 MB for each file.
Count: up to 500 fonts in one Brand Kit.
Rights: the font must allow embedding, and you must have the right to use it.
Free accounts cannot upload custom fonts at all.

blocks.text: Which font files Canva accepts

The file format is where most uploads fail. Canva wants static fonts in OTF, TTF or WOFF form. It does not take a ZIP archive, even one that holds the right fonts. It also rejects WOFF2, EOT, SVG fonts and variable fonts. A variable font packs many weights into one file, so you may need the static files that come with the same family. Check the download page from your font source for a static version.

blocks.caption: Upload limits as listed by cofonts and KeepCanva in 2026.

blocks.text: Get the font file ready on your Mac

Finder is where most font files start on a Mac. They arrive in Downloads, inside a ZIP from a designer, or as an attachment from a foundry. Open the file before you upload it. Apple's Font Book app checks each font for errors. It also warns you about duplicates, and it offers to keep both, skip or replace.

Keep the names the font came with. KeepCanva advises against renaming files before upload. cofonts also reports that styles can split into separate fonts when names change. A file named by its foundry is safer than one you rename by hand. Copy the files into one clean folder so you can find them again.
Upload every style, or Bold and Italic stay grey

This problem looks like a bug, but it is a missing file. If you upload only the Regular file, the B and I buttons in Canva stay greyed out. Canva treats each style as its own file. Upload the Bold and Italic files too, if the family has them. cofonts also says fonts uploaded before July 2023 may need to be uploaded again to group together.
What to do when Canva says Something went wrong

That message is a catch-all. Canva uses the same text for many different failures, so it does not tell you which one you hit. Work through the likely causes in order. Start with the format and the license, because they cause most rejections. Then check size, names, your role and the cache.

items: Wrong format: extract the ZIP and upload the OTF, TTF or WOFF file inside it.
Licensing rejection: get a version of the font licensed for embedding.
Unreadable file: download the font again, because the file may be corrupt.
Too large: ask the source for a version under 15 MB.
Naming error: check the family and style names in Font Book.
Missing Upload button: confirm your role is owner, admin or brand designer.
Stale page: refresh the page or clear your browser cache, then try again.
Duplicate style: upload only the styles that are new to the Brand Kit.

blocks.text: Adobe fonts and the older Finder workaround

If your font came from Adobe Fonts, you may find older advice about copying files out of a hidden Adobe folder. Frocks in Stock describes that workaround in a post from 2023, updated in 2025. Both cofonts and KeepCanva say Adobe Originals fonts are not supported for upload. Treat the workaround as unreliable. It also says nothing about the license, and the license is the question that matters. Check your Adobe terms before you copy anything from a hidden folder.
Check the font after the upload finishes

Once the font appears in your Brand Kit, test it in a real design. Open a blank design, add a text box, and open the font menu. Search for the family name. If the font is missing from the list, the upload may have stalled, or you picked the wrong category.

Then test the B and I buttons. Those show whether the Bold and Italic files arrived. Export a PNG and open it in Preview, the image app that comes with macOS, to check the letters. If the export looks wrong, check that the design uses the font you uploaded, not a similar font Canva substituted.
Common mistakes that waste an afternoon

items: Uploading a ZIP file and waiting for it to change.
Renaming files to make them look tidy before the upload.
Trying to upload on a Free plan and blaming the font.
Uploading one style and expecting the whole family to work.
Skipping the license check because the upload finished.
Copying Adobe files out of a hidden folder without checking the license.

blocks.text: How uploaded fonts are shared in a team

A font goes into the Brand Kit, not into one design. The kit is where a team keeps its shared fonts. One guide says uploaded fonts sync to any device where you are signed in. Canva's own pages did not confirm that for this guide. Test it on a second device before you tell your team it works.
When the font list will not refresh

If a clean upload still doesn't show, the app may be holding an old copy of the font list. Quit Canva with ⌘Q, reopen it, and check the font menu again. If it still fails, the [reset guide](/how-to/reset-the-desktop-app-in-canva) covers a clean restart of the desktop app. If you have not installed the desktop app yet, the [install guide](/how-to/download-and-install-canva-in-canva) shows the steps.
Next steps once your font works

Save a template that uses the new font, so your next design starts with it. Before you change a live design, make a copy first. The [duplicate guide](/how-to/duplicate-a-design-in-canva) shows how to copy a design in Canva on Mac. Keep the original font files in one folder, labeled by family, so you can upload them again after a reinstall.

faq.question: Can I upload a font to Canva for free?
faq.answer: No. cofonts says Canva's Free plan cannot upload custom fonts. You need Canva Pro or a team plan. Check your current plan in Canva before you start, because the guides disagree on whether Business counts.

faq.question: Why does Canva say Something went wrong when I upload a font?
faq.answer: That message is a catch-all for several failures. The usual causes are an unsupported format, a font that is not licensed for embedding, a corrupt download, a file over 15 MB, a naming error, a missing role, a stale cache or a duplicate style. Start with the format and the license.

faq.question: Does uploading a font work differently on a Mac than on Windows?
faq.answer: Not in the sources I could check. KeepCanva does not describe a platform difference in the upload itself. The Mac part is preparing the file in Finder and checking it in Font Book. Canva's own help pages could not be opened for this guide, so check them if a label differs.

faq.question: Which font file types does Canva accept?
faq.answer: OTF, TTF and WOFF files, and only static ones. Canva rejects ZIP archives, WOFF2, EOT, SVG fonts and variable fonts. Each file must be under 15 MB, according to KeepCanva.

faq.question: Why are Bold and Italic greyed out after I upload a font?
faq.answer: Usually the Bold or Italic file is missing from the Brand Kit. Upload each style as its own file, keep the original file names, then reopen the font menu in your design.

faq.question: If I install a font in Font Book, will it show up in Canva?
faq.answer: None of the sources I checked confirm that. Apple's Font Book guide covers installing fonts on your Mac, but it does not mention Canva. Upload the font through the Brand Kit to be sure it appears there.

faq.question: Can I upload Adobe fonts to Canva?
faq.answer: Not as Adobe Originals. cofonts and KeepCanva both say Adobe Originals fonts are not supported. Older Finder workarounds exist, but they do not settle the license question, so don't rely on them.

faq.question: How many fonts can one Brand Kit hold?
faq.answer: Up to 500 fonts per Brand Kit, according to cofonts and KeepCanva. Once you reach the limit, you need to remove a font before you can upload another.

task: Upload a custom font to Canva on a Mac
appliesTo: Canva paid plans on a Mac, in the browser or the desktop app
requirements: Canva Pro, Teams, Education or Nonprofits plan
Owner, admin or brand designer role
Static OTF, TTF or WOFF font file
Font file under 15 MB, licensed for embedding

steps.name: Check your plan and role
steps.text: Sign in to Canva in your browser or the Canva desktop app, using the account that holds the paid plan. Uploads need Canva Pro, Teams, Education or Nonprofits, and one guide also lists Business. Your role must be owner, admin or brand designer. If you cannot see an Upload option, your role is the most likely reason.
steps.tip: Free accounts cannot upload custom fonts, so a role change will not help on the Free plan.

steps.name: Find the font file in Finder
steps.text: Open Finder and go to the folder where the font landed, often Downloads. Use the static OTF, TTF or WOFF file for each style. If you have a ZIP, double-click it to extract it, then keep the font files and ignore the rest. Confirm each file is under 15 MB by checking its size in Get Info.
steps.tip: Do not rename the file. Keep the name the foundry gave it.

steps.name: Optional: validate the font in Font Book
steps.text: Double-click the font file in Finder to open its preview in Font Book. Click Install if you want macOS to validate it. Font Book checks each font for errors and warns about duplicates. Installing is optional for Canva, and none of the sources I checked confirm that a Font Book install puts a font into Canva.
steps.tip: If Font Book reports an error, fix the file before you upload it to Canva.

steps.name: Open Brand and pick your Brand Kit
steps.text: In Canva, find the left sidebar and click Brand. Some pages and guides call this Brand Kit. Pick the Brand Kit you want the font in. The sidebar labels differ across guides, so match what you see on screen rather than what a guide shows.
steps.tip: If you see only one kit, Canva may open it straight away.

steps.name: Open the Fonts section
steps.text: Inside the Brand Kit, click Fonts. KeepCanva calls this section Brand Fonts. If you want the font grouped with others, such as a heading family, click Add to category and pick or create a category. The category step comes before the upload in the guides.
steps.tip: Set up the category first so the font lands in the right group.

steps.name: Click Upload a font and choose your file
steps.text: Click Upload a font. Canva opens a file picker, or you can drag the file from Finder onto the upload area. Select your OTF, TTF or WOFF file. Repeat this for each style file, one at a time, so every style is listed under the family.
steps.tip: Add the Bold and Italic files now, or the B and I buttons will stay greyed out.

steps.name: Confirm you have the right to use the font
steps.text: Canva asks you to confirm you have the right to use the font before the upload finishes. Read the license first. The font must allow embedding, and your team must be allowed to use it in designs. If the license only covers personal use, do not upload it to a team Brand Kit.
steps.tip: Keep a copy of the license in the same folder as the font file.

steps.name: Wait for the upload to finish
steps.text: Stay on the page until the upload completes and the font appears under Brand Fonts or the category you chose. Large files take longer. If the font does not appear, refresh the page and look again. Do not start a second upload of the same file while the first one runs.
steps.tip: One guide says uploaded fonts sync to every device you are signed in on. Test that on a second device.

steps.name: Test the font in a design
steps.text: Open a design or start a blank one. Add a text box, open the font menu, and search for the family name. Select it and type a few words. Then test the Bold and Italic buttons. If they stay grey, the matching style file is missing from the Brand Kit.
steps.tip: Export a PNG and open it in Preview to see the font as it will look in print or online.

troubleshooting.problem: The Upload a font button is missing
troubleshooting.fix: Confirm your role is owner, admin or brand designer. Ask your team admin to check your role if you are not sure.
Work through the format, license, size and name checks in the section above, starting with the file format.

troubleshooting.problem: Bold or Italic is greyed out after upload
troubleshooting.fix: Upload the Bold or Italic file as its own file, then reopen the font menu in your design.

troubleshooting.problem: The font does not appear after upload
troubleshooting.fix: Refresh the page or quit Canva with ⌘Q and reopen it. Then check the category you picked in the Fonts section.
